activities.title: Listening walk
parentPrompts: Take a short walk inside or outside. Stop and be very quiet for a few moments, just listening.
Ask: "What did you hear?" Help them with describing words: loud, quiet, high, low, buzzing, tapping.
Make a sound yourself, such as tapping a cup or crinkling paper, and ask them to describe it.
Take turns: they make a sound with their eyes closed and you describe it.

activities.title: Same or different?
parentPrompts: Say two words that sound almost the same, such as "cat" and "cap." Ask: "Are they the same word or different words?"
Try pairs like bat/bat, pig/big, ship/sip, and sock/sock. Cover your mouth so they listen instead of watching your lips.
Let them make up pairs for you to judge.
Say a word wrong on purpose ("sock" for "rock") and let them catch the silly mistake.

activities.title: Feel the letters
materials: a thin layer of salt, sand, or cornmeal
parentPrompts: Spread the salt or cornmeal on the tray. Wash hands afterward, and keep it out of mouths and eyes.
Write a letter with your finger and ask: "Do you know this letter?" Name it together.
Let them trace over it with their finger, then try writing their own. Smooth the tray to start again.
Start with letters from their name, then add one or two new ones each time.

activities.title: Silly sound sentences
materials: a few small objects that start with the same sound, such as sock, sun, and spoon
parentPrompts: Show the objects and say each one, stretching the first sound: "sssock, sssun, sssspoon."
Ask: "What sound do they all start with?"
Make a silly sentence together: "Sammy sees seven silly socks."
Let them pick a new sound and hunt for objects that start with it.

activities.title: Read about the five senses
materials: a picture book about the senses
parentPrompts: Read the book, pausing to point at pictures. Ask: "What can we see here? What might it smell like?"
Name the five senses together and tap the body part for each: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands.
Ask: "Which sense do you like best? Why?"
After the book, ask them to tell you something they learned.

activities.title: Count the taps
materials: a spoon and a pot, or a drum
parentPrompts: Count from 1 to 10 together while you tap the pot with each number.
Tap a few times while they close their eyes. Ask: "How many taps did you hear?" Tap again slowly so they can count.
Switch: they tap and you count. Sometimes make a mistake and let them catch it.
Try loud taps and soft taps. Count each kind separately.

activities.title: Touch box sort
materials: a few objects that feel different, such as a cotton ball, sandpaper, a smooth stone, and a soft cloth
parentPrompts: Put one object in the bag. Ask them to reach in without looking and describe how it feels.
Reveal it and talk about it: "Was it rough or smooth? Soft or hard?"
Sort the objects into two groups, such as rough and smooth.
Ask: "How are these alike? How are they different?" Keep small objects out of mouths.

activities.title: Numbers 6 to 10
materials: index cards with the numerals 6 to 10 written on them
small objects like blocks or large buttons
parentPrompts: Lay out the cards in order and say each number. Ask them to point to the number you say.
Hold up a card and have them build a group of that many objects. Count together to check.
Show a group and ask them to find the matching card.
Play "what comes next?" by pointing to 6, 7, 8 and pausing.

activities.title: More or fewer?
materials: about 20 snack pieces such as banana slices or cereal rings
parentPrompts: Check for food allergies first. Skip hard or round foods that are a choking risk, like whole grapes or nuts.
Put a different number of snack pieces on each plate, using 10 or fewer. Ask: "Which plate has more? Which has fewer?"
Count each plate to check. Then line the pieces up in pairs to see which has extras.
Change the amounts and ask again. Let them eat the extras at the end.

activities.title: Patterns with textures
materials: two kinds of fabric or paper squares, such as felt and sandpaper
parentPrompts: Start a pattern: rough, smooth, rough, smooth. Ask: "What comes next?"
Let them continue the pattern and touch each piece as they go.
Try a new pattern: rough, rough, smooth, rough, rough, smooth.
Take turns making a pattern for each other to continue.

activities.title: Texture rubbings
materials: things with texture like leaves, coins, and a tile
parentPrompts: Place a leaf or coin under the paper and rub the side of a crayon across it until the shape appears.
Try different objects. Ask: "What do you notice? Which pattern is bumpy?"
Let them arrange their rubbings into a collage.
Ask them to describe their favorite texture.

activities.title: Paint to music
parentPrompts: Play a slow song and ask them to move the brush or crayon the way the music feels.
Switch to a fast song. Notice how the lines change.
Ask: "What did the music make you want to draw?"
Hang the artwork and let them tell you about it.

activities.title: Cinnamon playdough
parentPrompts: Check for allergies first. This is for smelling and squishing, not for eating.
Knead a pinch of cinnamon into the playdough together. Ask: "What do you smell?"
Roll, pinch, and shape the dough. Describe how it feels.
Make something together: a snake, a ball, or a bowl.

activities.title: Mix colors
materials: washable paint in red, yellow, and blue
parentPrompts: Put a small blob of two colors on the plate. Ask: "What do you think will happen if we mix them?"
Mix with a finger or brush and look at what appears. Try red and yellow, then blue and yellow.
Name the new colors together.
Paint a picture using the colors you made.

activities.title: Draw what you hear
materials: a jar with a few dry beans or rice, taped shut
parentPrompts: Have your child close their eyes while you shake the sealed jar, tap a table, or crinkle paper.
Ask them to draw what the sound makes them think of.
Talk about it: "Was it loud? Was it fast? What does it look like?"
Switch: you draw what you hear while they make the sound.
